The *Samuddakākajātaka* (Ja 146) is a tale within the Jātaka collection of the Pali canon. According to its traditional opening account, the story opens with the phrase "Our throats are tired" and was delivered by the Buddha while residing at Jetavana. The narrative concerns a group of elderly monks who, in their prior lay life, were wealthy companions and squires of Sāvatthī; inspired after listening to the Buddha preach during their performance of good works, they renounced home and household life in their advanced years to seek an end to sorrow within the monastic order.
